evidence_note: This pack does NOT contain sMewa or sPar-kha construction rules. It documents what this pass actually established by direct retrieval and direct visual inspection of the primary source: (1) the White Beryl (bai DUr dkar po) and its companion clarificatory treatise (bai DUr g.ya' sel) are both public-domain, fully retrievable, and their elemental-astrology (byung-rtsis/nag-rtsis) chapter block is real and locatable, which makes the previously-recorded 'no sourced anchor' / licensing framing for sMewa and sPar-kha FALSE as a rights/access claim, in the same pattern as false blockers already dissolved elsewhere in this repository (Nahuatl Florentine Codex, CC-BY-SA Arabic/Latin texts). (2) A genuine, different blocker remains: this specific print could not be read to sentence-level transcription confidence in this pass, which is an evidentiary-quality/paleography gate, not a rights gate. No rule here should be read as asserting any numeric mewa/parkha value, cycle direction, or delineation - none was verified. STATUS NUANCE (this field is a closed enum and cannot carry it): the rules in this manifest are provenance and boundary findings - source identity, rights determination, chapter location, the legibility reclassification, and the cross-tradition separation discipline - and those are verified. NO sMewa or sPar-kha CONSTRUCTION rule is present, because none could be extracted at defensibility grade from the available photostat witness. Do not read 'research_verified' as meaning the elemental layer is encoded; it is not. The prior value of this field was 'access_established_extraction_not_yet_reliable', which said so plainly but was not schema-legal.

exceptions: Keyword-hit clustering is a locator heuristic built on an OCR text layer already shown elsewhere in this pack to be unreliable; it is treated as evidence of WHERE to look, not as evidence of WHAT the passages say.

conditions.observation: Tibetan byung-rtsis/nag-rtsis (sMewa, sPar-kha) ultimately draws its numerological apparatus - a nine-number magic square and eight trigrams - from the same Chinese five-phase/Yijing-derived cosmological substrate that also underlies the Japanese Onmyodo shikiban tradition and (via a wholly separate Indian/Buddhist transmission for its own core units) is explicitly NOT shared with Sukuyodo's 27-mansion system

conclusion.ruling: this track shares no source, no rule, and no vector with docs/research/multitradition/onmyodo/, docs/research/multitradition/sukuyodo/, or docs/research/multitradition/bazi/, despite the distant common Chinese numerological root with Onmyodo/BaZi. The Tibetan corpus, transmission history, technical vocabulary (Wylie Tibetan, not Chinese or Japanese), and institutional context (Men-Tsee-Khang/Phugpa lineage) are distinct and no value may be inherited across tracks

exceptions: A rgya-rtsis rnying-ma (old-Chinese-derived) versus rgya-rtsis gsar-ma (new-Chinese-derived) distinction is itself internal to the Tibetan taxonomy per Men-Tsee-Khang and is preserved, not flattened, by this rule.
